findings.evidence: The comparison paragraph reports the 10-DM model sensitivity as 0.925, while the Results (p.3) and Abstract report sensitivity 0.854 for test set 1 and 0.905 for external test set 2. 0.925 is not reported for the 10-DM model anywhere else in the paper.

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' / 'Prognostic model' vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb code cell 8 and code/GC-prognosis-model/run.ipynb code cell (CI function)
findings.evidence: Paper reports 95% CIs for AUROC (0.944-0.987 test set 1; 0.697-0.951 prognostic test set). The CI function in both notebooks takes the 5th and 95th percentiles of the bootstrap AUROCs (confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05*len)], confidence_upper = sorted_scores[int(0.95*len)]) and its own comment says 'You can change the bounds percentiles to 0.025 and 0.975 to get a 95% confidence interval instead' — i.e. the computed interval is a 90% interval. Stored output prints [0.941 - 0.986] (test set 1) and [0.697 - 0.951] (prognostic test set).
